implementation_principle: PCA achieves dimensionality reduction by projecting high-dimensional data onto low-dimensional principal components with maximum variance through linear transformation
GLMPCA models raw counts using Poisson or negative binomial likelihoods and employs bias residuals for rapid approximate computation
pCMF achieves dimensionality reduction by probabilistically decomposing data through a sparse Gamma-Poisson factor model
ZIFA maps high-dimensional data to a low-dimensional space by introducing factor analysis with a zero-inflation model
reference: (“ZIFA: Dimensionality reduction for zero-inflated single-cell gene expression analysis,” n.d.)

implementation_principle: scGBM directly models data through a Poisson bilinear model, achieving dimensionality reduction by introducing a low-dimensional factor structure in the log-mean representation

SSNMDI projects high-dimensional data onto a low-dimensional space through non-negative matrix factorization, integrating data interpolation and label information within the framework to optimize dimensionality reduction
tGPLVM maps high-dimensional data to low dimensions via Gaussian processes and models noise using a heavy-tailed t-distribution
VAE maps high-dimensional data to a low-dimensional latent distribution via an encoder, then reconstructs it using a decoder to maximize the ELBO for dimensionality reduction
scvis combines variational autoencoders with t-SNE regularization to learn a probabilistic mapping function for dimensionality reduction
VASC employs a deep variational autoencoder for dimensionality reduction and utilizes a ZI layer to handle dropout events
SAUCIE employs a deep autoencoder with multiple regularization terms to simultaneously accomplish tasks such as dimensionality reduction, denoising, and clustering
scScope employs a deep recurrent autoencoder to iteratively repair missing values in scRNA-seq data while simultaneously performing batch normalization and feature learning
SCDRHA first applies DCA for denoising, then employs a graph attention autoencoder for dimensionality reduction
scGAE achieves dimensionality reduction by constructing cell maps and using graph autoencoders
DREAM employs a combination of variational autoencoders and mixture of Gaussians for dimensionality reduction of scRNA-seq data, utilizing a ZI layer to handle dropout events
DRA employs adversarial variational autoencoders for dimensionality reduction
UMAP achieves nonlinear dimensionality reduction by constructing a proximity graph in high-dimensional space and optimizing low-dimensional embeddings to preserve its neighborhood structure.
SIMLR adaptively learns the optimal similarity matrix between cells through multi-core learning, utilizing this matrix for dimensionality reduction.
PHATE performs dimensionality reduction through multidimensional scaling analysis while preserving geometric information by constructing the diffusion geometry of the data.
EDGE constructs an inter-cell similarity matrix by integrating numerous weak learners and performs dimensionality reduction based on this matrix.
SPDR achieves dimension reduction that preserves data structure while correcting batch effects by cross-batch sampling triplets and optimizing the loss function.
Ivis employs a concatenated neural network and triplet loss to map high-dimensional data to low dimensions while supporting rapid embedding of new data points.

PaCMAP preserves the neighborhood structure of data while performing dimensionality reduction by constructing three types of point pairs: nearest neighbors, intermediate neighbors, and distant neighbors.

t-SNE transforms the similarity between high-dimensional points into probability distributions and matches these distributions in a low-dimensional space to achieve dimensionality reduction while preserving structural information.
TriMap learns low-dimensional embeddings by sampling triplet constraints from high-dimensional data and optimizing the loss function.
SQuadMDS randomly groups data into quadruplets and utilizes gradient descent to optimize relative distance error, achieving multidimensional scaling with linear complexity.
